summary: Earth Intelligence Platform is a web platform we built that turns open NASA Earth-observation data into decisions people can trust. It has two modules on one shared data layer: Climate Research (NASA POWER time series, Earthdata CMR search, NASA GIBS satellite layers, and drought and heat indicators such as SPI, SPEI, heatwaves and frost days) and Farmer Assistant (FAO-56 irrigation advice in mm and m³/day, risk alerts, and a daily “what should I do today?” plan). Every result shows its data source, formula, confidence score and limitations, and the platform never invents data. This matters because NASA data is free but hard to use; we turn it into clear, explainable actions for farmers and climate researchers, in Persian and English.
details:
Earth Intelligence Platform – Project Details

Earth Intelligence Platform is a bilingual web-based platform that transforms open Earth observation and climate data into reliable, understandable, and actionable information for climate researchers and farmers.

The platform consists of two integrated modules built on a shared data infrastructure:

1. Climate Research: Provides access to NASA POWER climate time series, NASA Earthdata Common Metadata Repository (CMR) search, and NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) satellite imagery. It integrates satellite-based indicators, including MODIS Terra/Aqua NDVI, EVI, Land Surface Temperature, True Color, and SMAP soil moisture layers. It also supports climate analysis through drought and extreme-weather indicators such as SPI, SPEI, heatwaves, and frost days.

2. Farmer Assistant: Provides practical agricultural guidance, including FAO-56-based irrigation recommendations in millimeters and cubic meters per day, environmental risk alerts, and a daily action plan answering: "What should I do today?"

The platform combines satellite observations, climate data, geospatial services, and agricultural datasets to make complex scientific information accessible. Each result aims to provide its data source, calculation method, confidence level, and limitations to support transparency and prevent unsupported conclusions.

The project was developed using Python, Django, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and geospatial web services.

Its main innovation is connecting scientific Earth observation data with practical agricultural decision-making through a single bilingual platform. The intended impact is to support smarter water management, improve agricultural planning, increase climate awareness, and help researchers and farmers make better-informed decisions.
